I emit WPL-AI plans — I'm not built to answer programming-theory questions in prose. But I can encode this as a plan: a light testing session that uses submaximal markers (bar speed proxies, RPE at fixed loads, rep-quality benchmarks) instead of true maxes, so it doesn't break the deload.

Quick framing before the plan: don't test 1RM, don't go above RPE 7, don't add sets on top of the deload week. The cleanest in-deload markers are **fixed-load RPE checks** on the main lifts — pick a load he's hit cleanly before, do a single set, log RPE and rep quality. If RPE drops vs prior weeks at the same load, recovery is landing.

I'd slot it onto an existing day rather than add a session. Here's the week with a testing block folded into Saturday (replacing Full Body Flush, since that day was the lightest and most flexible):

How to read the test day: each lift is **one** working set at a fixed load he's used recently (pick something around his prior 75–80% 1RM), targeted at RPE 7. The marker isn't the weight — it's the RPE he reports at that fixed load, and bar speed/rep quality. If RPE comes in at 6 or below, deload is working and he's primed for intensification. If it's 8+, he's not recovered and the next block needs to start lighter.

I'd push back on this one before emitting. The whole point of the deload is what comes after it — the intensification block. Cutting it short because he feels good on Wednesday is exactly when deloads get wasted. "Feeling great by Wednesday" is the deload working, not evidence it's done.

Boredom isn't a programming signal. If you ramp Wed/Fri, you've effectively run a 2-day deload, and he goes into intensification with residual fatigue you can't see until week 2 or 3 of the next block — usually as a stall or a tweak.

That said, you're the trainer and you know him. Two options I'll emit cleanly:

**Option A (recommended): keep the deload, redirect the boredom.** Add some skill/quality work he can attack mentally without adding fatigue — tempo work, pause reps, unilateral, light technique focus. Same RPE ceiling.

**Option B: bump Wed and Fri as requested.** I'll do it, but Wed stays a mobility/quality day (pushing a mobility session into hard work defeats its purpose — I'll convert it to a proper lifting day) and Fri becomes moderate intensity, not full send. Hard cap RPE 7. Anything higher and you're not deloading.

Tell me which. If you don't reply, I'll default to A — it's the one that protects the next block.

I'm a WPL-AI emitter — I output plan documents, not summary prose. I can't cleanly give you a table or analysis breakdown in my output format.

What I can do: re-emit the current plan so you can read it end-to-end, or encode a summary as plan metadata (goal names, session titles) if that's useful. Tell me which.

Quick orientation though, since you asked: the week as it stands is 7 days, 7 sessions — Mon push, Tue lower, Wed mobility, Thu pull, Fri Z2 cardio, Sat submaximal strength test, Sun Z2 cardio. Lifting volume is ~2 sets per exercise vs his prior ~18 sets/session (roughly 55–60% volume cut on compounds, more on isolation). Intensity is RPE 6 on main lifts vs his prior 8.5 (about 2.5 RPE points down, which maps to ~15–20% load reduction at matched reps). Test day Saturday is the only RPE 7 work in the week, and it's single sets.

If you want that as a proper deliverable, I'd need it in a format I emit — say the word and I'll regenerate the plan, or we move on to building the intensification block.
